text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated 5xx and gateway timeouts detected on /v1/generate across us-east-1. Error rate jump from 0.2% -> 6.8% over 60s. Batching scheduler queue depth rising, head-of-line growth observed. Auto-page oncall.

oncall-bot: Paging alyssa (oncall) — severity: Sev2. Escalation timer started.

alyssa: got it, looking. Any customer-facing pages yet?

jordan: yes — throughput to a handful of high-traffic tenants dropped, some 504s reported through the gateway. Support reported ~3 customers with increased latency.

alyssa: ok. First things first: is this a single region thing? metrics?

samir: it's us-east-1 primarily, small blip in eu-west. Batcher queue length on runtime-batcher-1 up from 500 -> 4200 in last 5m. Scheduler logs show long scheduling latency (~1.1s -> 9.8s).

alyssa: this looks like a head-of-line queue buildup causing timeouts at the gateway. Priority: mitigate customer impact, then debug root cause.

kevin: repeating errors in logs: 
```
ERROR scheduler: failed to schedule batch: timeout waiting for executor (waited 20s)
WARN runtime: kv-cache miss spike, prefetch thrash
```

maya: any recent deploys?

jordan: no deploys in last 30m. Autoscaler made a few scale attempts but pods stuck terminating -> creating loops on the batcher nodes.

alyssa: immediate mitigation plan:
1) Put gateway into limited ingress mode for low-tier routes (throttle)
2) Spin up emergency batcher capacity in a different AZ / fallback pool
3) Enable preemptive eviction on long-waiting queues (>8s)
4) Route high-priority keys to a dedicated fast-path

samir: commands to run:
```bash
# throttle low tier routes
redwoodctl routes throttle --selector tier=free --rate 10r/s --region us-east-1
# scale fallback pool
kubectl scale deployment/batcher-fallback -n inference --replicas=8
# enable eviction
redwoodctl scheduler set --eviction-threshold 8s --mode preemptive
```

alyssa: executing now. I'll start throttle and scale fallback. Jordan take routing and ensure canary model fallback enabled.

jordan: on it. Enabling model-fallback for heavy routes and switching route priority for tenant-blacklist.

oncall-bot: alyssa acknowledged the page.

alyssa: throttle applied to free-tier routes. fallback batchers scaling (expected join ~45s). preemptive eviction toggled on.

samir: seeing batcher-fallback pods coming up in AZ b, join rate good. queue depth dropping from 4200 -> 1800 now. 5xx rate falling to 2.1%.

maya: adding a quick KV cache check — can someone run kvstats on the busiest nodes?

kevin: running kvstats:
```
kvstats --node runtime-014 --window 60s
# results: miss-rate 42%, eviction-rate spike correlated with scheduler latency
```

alyssa: interesting — KV miss/eviction thrash likely exacerbated scheduling. Could be memory pressure / GC on nodes. Jordan, can you check pod OOMs or GC logs?

jordan: checking pods: a few batcher-worker pods restarted repeatedly, OOMKilled on containerd logs around the same time as the spike. GC cycles long on runtime-014. Might be a memory leak in the latest quantization path.

alyssa: ok. rollback option: pin affected routes to older model variant (quantization disabled) while we debug. Jordan, flip the routing.

jordan: routing switch complete for top 5 tenants -> pinned to model-v1.9-no-quant. Confirming route propagation.

samir: post-switch, error rate down to 0.7% and queue depth ~300. Gateway 504s near zero. Looks like rollback helped.

oncall-bot: Incident summary update: mitigation applied — throttles, fallback pool, eviction, model fallback. Customer impact reduced.

alyssa: good. Next: capture heap/pprof from affected pods, collect recent scheduler logs, and open an eval to reproduce the quantization path memory growth. Jordan/Samir take lead on debugging.

jordan: capturing pprof now. Uploading to /shared/incidents/5181234567/pprof.tgz

samir: I'll grab scheduler trace and kv-cache traces.

maya: i'll prepare customer comms draft: short note to affected tenants about transient 5xx and remediation steps, offer follow-up.

alyssa: also notify SRE + runtime-ml team, mark this for postmortem and model-onboarding review. Assigning follow-ups:
- jordan: collect logs + run reproducer (owner)
- samir: KV cache and scheduler trace (owner)
- kevin: reproduce memory growth in staging (owner)
- maya: customer comm and outreach (owner)

kevin: quick question — do we want to revert the quantization rollout entirely for now?

alyssa: yes, temporarily retract rollout. I'll submit the rollback.

incident-bot: Rollback of quantization rollout initiated by alyssa — tracking issue #INC-5181.

samir: confirming no active paging alerts left. metrics stabilizing. I'll keep an eye for 30m before marking resolved.

maya: posting customer note draft for review: "We experienced a transient increase in errors/timeouts in us-east-1 due to a scheduler/batcher congestion triggered by a model quantization path. We mitigated by throttling low-priority traffic and routing high-usage tenants to a stable model variant. No data loss. We're investigating root cause and will follow up."

alyssa: fine to send after minor edits. Jordan/Samir stay on debug — handover to maya at +3h for monitoring. If anything spikes re-page.

jordan: capturing reproducer logs, attaching commands used to test:
```bash
# synthetic load to reproduce
ab -n 20000 -c 60 -p payload.json https://gateway.us-east-1.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

kevin: starting memory repro in staging, will report in the triage ticket.

alyssa: thank you all. Great mitigation run — fallback pool + model pin did the trick. Leaving a short runbook for oncall:
- If queue depth > 1500 and 5xx > 1.5%: throttle free-tier, scale batcher-fallback, enable preemptive eviction, pin heavy tenants to stable model
- If OOMs present: take affected nodes out of rotation and scale fallback

samir: noted and added to runbook.

oncall-bot: Incident marked as mitigated. Monitoring window 30m.

maya: i'll take over monitoring and customer comms. filing follow-ups to engineering teams for root cause and postmortem.

alyssa: handing off. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

maya: handoff accepted.

incident-bot: Thread closed for active mitigation; follow-up ticket link: https://issues.redwood.ai/INC-5181
